task_3.title: Expose proxy tunneling state on connections
task_3.description: urllib3 2.3.0 adds a public connection property for determining whether an HTTP or HTTPS connection is configured to use proxy tunneling. The existing HTTPS connection tunnel decision should continue to behave the same while using the newly exposed state.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that users can inspect whether an HTTPConnection or HTTPSConnection is configured for proxy tunneling through a public property.

expectation.grounded: Add a `proxy_is_tunneling` boolean property to `HTTPConnection` and make it available on `HTTPSConnection` through inheritance. The property should return true when the connection has a configured proxy tunnel target and false otherwise. HTTPS connection setup should use this public tunneling state when deciding whether to establish a proxy tunnel.
expectation.conceptual: Connection objects should expose whether they are using a tunneling proxy, allowing callers to distinguish tunnel-based proxying from non-tunneled or absent proxy usage without relying on private connection details.

constraints.grounded: `proxy_is_tunneling` must not change the existing semantics of `proxy_is_forwarding`, connection closing, proxy verification, or HTTPS tunnel establishment. HTTPS connections that previously established a tunnel must still do so, and connections without a tunnel target must not be treated as tunneled.
constraints.conceptual: The new inspection capability should be additive and should not alter existing proxy behavior or break current forwarding-proxy detection.

behavior: `HTTPConnection.proxy_is_tunneling` returns false when no proxy tunnel target is configured.
`HTTPConnection.proxy_is_tunneling` returns true when a proxy tunnel target is configured.
`HTTPSConnection` exposes the same `proxy_is_tunneling` property.
`HTTPSConnection` uses the tunneling state to decide whether to establish an HTTP CONNECT-style tunnel before connecting to the origin.
Existing `proxy_is_forwarding` behavior remains distinct: forwarding proxy state and tunneling proxy state are reported separately.
acceptance_criteria: Given an `HTTPConnection` without a configured tunnel target, when `proxy_is_tunneling` is read, it should return false.
Given an `HTTPConnection` configured to tunnel through a proxy, when `proxy_is_tunneling` is read, it should return true.
Given an `HTTPSConnection`, when `proxy_is_tunneling` is read, it should expose the same tunnel-state semantics as `HTTPConnection`.
When an HTTPS connection is configured for proxy tunneling, it should still follow the existing tunnel establishment flow.
When an HTTPS connection is not configured for proxy tunneling, it should not enter the tunnel establishment flow solely because a proxy exists.
When a connection is configured for proxy forwarding instead of proxy tunneling, `proxy_is_forwarding` and `proxy_is_tunneling` should remain distinguishable.

task_5.title: Correct HTTP version in debug logs
task_5.description: The update fixes urllib3 connection pool debug logging so completed request lines render the formatted HTTP protocol version correctly, addressing cases where HTTP/1.1 appeared without its decimal separator.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that urllib3 debug logs for completed HTTP requests display the response HTTP version in its correctly formatted protocol form.

expectation.grounded: When urllib3.connectionpool emits the completed-request debug log from HTTPConnectionPool after receiving a response, the request line should use the response's formatted version string, such as the HTTP/1.1 representation, instead of deriving the protocol token from the raw numeric response version. The logged scheme, host, port, method, URL, status, and remaining length should continue to be emitted as before.
expectation.conceptual: Connection debug output should show the same HTTP version that users expect to see in a protocol line, including punctuation and formatting, while preserving the rest of the request summary.

constraints.grounded: Do not alter HTTPConnectionPool request execution, response objects, status handling, response length reporting, connection reuse, or whether debug logging is emitted. The change is limited to the formatted HTTP version field in the completed-request debug log.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should improve log accuracy only; it should not change network behavior, response semantics, or other log fields.

behavior: Completed-request debug logs emitted by urllib3.connectionpool now render HTTP/1.1 responses with the formatted HTTP/1.1 protocol token rather than the malformed HTTP/11 token.
The completed-request log line obtains the protocol/version text from the response's formatted version representation, so the displayed token matches the response's canonical version string.
The rest of the completed-request debug log remains unchanged, including scheme, host, port, method, URL, response status, and remaining response length.
acceptance_criteria: Given debug logging is enabled for urllib3.connectionpool and an HTTPConnectionPool request receives an HTTP/1.1 response, when the completed-request debug entry is emitted, it should display the protocol version as HTTP/1.1.
Given an HTTP/1.1 response, when the completed-request debug entry is emitted, it should not display the malformed protocol token HTTP/11.
When a completed-request debug entry is emitted, it should continue to include the same request and response summary fields besides the corrected HTTP version formatting.
When requests are made with debug logging disabled, request execution and response handling should behave the same as before.

task_6.title: Drop Python 3.8 support
task_6.description: urllib3 2.3.0 removes Python 3.8 support and updates runtime assumptions accordingly. The library may now rely on Python 3.9+ language and standard-library capabilities while preserving existing HTTP, header, request-field, and TLS behavior for supported runtimes.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that urllib3 no longer supports Python 3.8 and that runtime behavior assumes Python 3.9 or newer while preserving existing observable behavior for supported Python versions.

expectation.grounded: The library should remove Python 3.8 compatibility paths and may use Python 3.9+ built-in collection generics in runtime-evaluated type definitions. HTTPConnection connection creation should emit the standard http.client connection audit event through sys.audit on supported runtimes. create_urllib3_context should continue honoring a non-empty SSLKEYLOGFILE value by configuring SSLContext.keylog_filename, and SSL common-name reliability handling should no longer include CPython 3.8 as a supported fixed case.
expectation.conceptual: Users must run this release on Python 3.9 or newer. On supported runtimes, connection auditing, TLS key logging through the standard environment variable, SSL hostname-check behavior, request encoding, multipart fields, socket options, and header handling should continue to behave as before.

constraints.grounded: Do not retain compatibility behavior for missing sys.audit, CPython 3.8-specific SSL common-name handling, or missing SSLContext.keylog_filename when SSLKEYLOGFILE is set. Empty SSLKEYLOGFILE values should still be ignored. Public behavior for HTTPHeaderDict, request field inputs, multipart field inputs, socket options, exceptions, and request methods should not change on Python 3.9+ except for the intentional runtime baseline update.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should only remove obsolete Python runtime support. Existing urllib3 behavior for supported users should remain stable, and unsupported runtimes should not drive compatibility decisions.

behavior: Python 3.8 is no longer a supported runtime for urllib3 2.3.0.
Modules may rely on Python 3.9+ generic built-in collection syntax such as tuple, list, and set parameterization.
HTTP connection creation emits the standard Python HTTP client connection audit event through sys.audit without checking whether audit hooks exist.
SSL context creation reads SSLKEYLOGFILE and assigns SSLContext.keylog_filename when the value is non-empty.
An unset or empty SSLKEYLOGFILE value leaves TLS key logging disabled.
SSL common-name reliability detection no longer treats CPython 3.8.x as a supported fixed runtime; supported CPython fixed cases begin at 3.9.3 or newer.
Accepted shapes for header sources, multipart fields, URL-encoded fields, and socket options remain unchanged for supported Python versions.
acceptance_criteria: Given Python 3.9 or newer, importing urllib3 modules for connections, SSL utilities, header collections, request methods, exceptions, fields, file posting, and connection utilities should succeed.
When urllib3 establishes an HTTP connection on a supported runtime, it should emit the standard HTTP client connection audit event with the connection object, host, and port.
When SSLKEYLOGFILE is unset or empty, creating an urllib3 SSL context should not enable TLS key logging.
When SSLKEYLOGFILE is set to a non-empty value on a supported runtime, creating an urllib3 SSL context should configure the context to write TLS session keys to that value.
When determining SSL common-name reliability, CPython 3.9.3 and newer supported versions should be treated as fixed, while CPython 3.8 should not be treated as part of the supported runtime matrix.

When callers pass previously accepted header sources, multipart fields, URL-encoded fields, or socket options on Python 3.9 or newer, urllib3 should continue accepting those inputs with unchanged request behavior.
When a user attempts to use this release on Python 3.8, urllib3 should not promise import compatibility or runtime compatibility.

task_1.title: Add response read shutdown API
task_1.description: urllib3 2.3.0 adds a response-level shutdown operation so callers can explicitly stop ongoing or future reads for an individual HTTP response. This addresses streaming and multithreaded use cases where a reader can be blocked waiting on the socket and closing the response from another thread may not promptly interrupt that read.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that callers can explicitly interrupt ongoing or future reads for a single HTTP response without relying on closing the response to unblock a separate blocked reader.

expectation.grounded: Expose `shutdown()` on `BaseHTTPResponse` and `HTTPResponse`. For `HTTPResponse` instances backed by a connection socket that supports shutdown, calling `HTTPResponse.shutdown()` should perform read-side shutdown on the associated socket so blocked or later reads for that response are interrupted. If no socket shutdown operation is available, such as for responses constructed without connection socket support or after the response has been closed, `shutdown()` should raise `ValueError`. pyOpenSSL wrapped sockets should accept the same shutdown call shape and surface OpenSSL shutdown failures as `ssl.SSLError`.
expectation.conceptual: Streaming response objects provide a separate cancellation-style operation for read activity. The operation affects only the target response, interrupts pending or future reads where the transport supports it, and reports unsupported shutdown explicitly instead of silently doing nothing.

constraints.grounded: `HTTPResponse.close()` should continue to close response resources and should not be redefined as the read-interruption mechanism. Calling `shutdown()` must remain scoped to the response's associated socket and must not drain the response body, clear connection pools, or affect unrelated responses. Existing response reading and closing behavior should remain compatible aside from the new explicit shutdown capability.
constraints.conceptual: The new API should add a targeted way to stop reads without broad side effects. Normal response lifecycle operations should keep their existing meaning, and unsupported transports should fail clearly.

behavior: `BaseHTTPResponse` has a `shutdown()` method in its response interface.
`HTTPResponse.shutdown()` attempts to shut down the read side of the socket associated with that specific response.
A blocked read on a response whose socket is shut down through `HTTPResponse.shutdown()` should be interrupted by the underlying I/O failure instead of waiting indefinitely for more server data.
Calling `shutdown()` on an `HTTPResponse` without an available socket shutdown operation raises `ValueError`.
After `HTTPResponse.close()` has been called, the response no longer exposes an available socket shutdown operation through `shutdown()`.
pyOpenSSL socket wrappers accept a shutdown call with a shutdown mode argument and translate OpenSSL shutdown failures into `ssl.SSLError`.
acceptance_criteria: Given a streaming `HTTPResponse` from a connection-backed request, when another thread is blocked reading from that response and `shutdown()` is called on the response, then the blocked read should stop by surfacing an I/O or protocol-level read failure.

When `shutdown()` is called on a connection-backed `HTTPResponse`, it should target only that response's associated socket read direction and should not require closing or clearing the entire connection pool.
When `shutdown()` is called on a response that was not created with socket shutdown support, it should raise `ValueError`.
When `shutdown()` is called after the response has already been closed, it should raise `ValueError` rather than attempting another socket shutdown.
When urllib3 is using the pyOpenSSL socket wrapper, response shutdown should accept the same mode-based socket shutdown call and convert OpenSSL shutdown errors into `ssl.SSLError`.

task_2.title: Support JSPI fetch on Emscripten
task_2.description: urllib3's Emscripten transport now supports WebAssembly JavaScript Promise Integration so Pyodide can perform regular and streaming HTTP requests through JavaScript fetch more efficiently, including in Node.js when the runtime is launched with the required stack-switching support.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that urllib3 running on Emscripten/Pyodide can use JavaScript Promise Integration for both buffered and streaming HTTP requests, and can operate in Node.js when the runtime is configured for JSPI.

expectation.grounded: In urllib3.contrib.emscripten.fetch, expose JSPI availability through has_jspi(); when JSPI is available, send_request() and send_streaming_request() should route requests through a JS fetch-based path that returns an EmscriptenResponse with the request's status, response headers, and either buffered bytes or a readable raw stream. In Node.js, if JSPI is not available, request sending should fail with _RequestError that explains the Node.js runtime requirements instead of attempting the browser XMLHttpRequest or worker fallback. JSPI promise failures should map AbortError to _TimeoutError and other JavaScript exceptions to _RequestError.
expectation.conceptual: When the host runtime supports JSPI, urllib3 should make normal and streaming HTTP requests using the platform's asynchronous fetch API while presenting the same synchronous urllib3 response interface to Python callers. Node.js should work only when launched in a JSPI-capable mode, and unsupported Node.js configurations should fail clearly.

constraints.grounded: Preserve existing non-JSPI browser behavior, including the XMLHttpRequest path for non-streaming requests and the existing worker-based streaming fallback where applicable. Preserve request method, body, timeout, response status, response headers, and request/response context on urllib3 errors. Streaming response bodies returned by the JSPI path must behave as read-only, non-seekable raw streams and must close cleanly at EOF or when cancelled.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade must add JSPI support without regressing existing browser-based Emscripten usage. Unsupported runtimes should receive explicit urllib3 errors, while supported runtimes should see the same high-level request and response behavior they expect from urllib3.

behavior: has_jspi() reports whether Pyodide can synchronously wait on JavaScript promises through JSPI, and returns false when the required Pyodide support is unavailable.
send_request() uses the JSPI fetch path whenever JSPI is available and returns an EmscriptenResponse whose body is buffered bytes.
send_streaming_request() uses the JSPI fetch path whenever JSPI is available and returns an EmscriptenResponse whose body can be consumed incrementally as a raw readable stream.
In Node.js without usable JSPI, both regular and streaming request entry points raise _RequestError rather than falling back to browser-only transport mechanisms.
The JSPI fetch path propagates the request method, request body, allowed request headers, and abort signal to JavaScript fetch.
Response headers from JavaScript fetch are converted into the EmscriptenResponse headers mapping, and the fetch response status becomes the EmscriptenResponse status code.
A positive request timeout aborts the active fetch or stream read; an aborted JavaScript promise is surfaced as _TimeoutError.
Non-timeout JavaScript promise failures are surfaced as _RequestError with the relevant request and, when available, response context.
The JSPI streaming body reports readable as true, writable as false, and seekable as false; closing it cancels the JavaScript reader and releases request and response references.
When JSPI is unavailable outside Node.js, the existing Emscripten fallback behavior remains available.
acceptance_criteria: Given a Pyodide/Emscripten runtime where JSPI is available, when a caller makes a non-streaming urllib3 request, it should return an EmscriptenResponse with the fetch response status, headers, and buffered response bytes.

Given a Pyodide/Emscripten runtime where JSPI is available, when a caller makes a streaming urllib3 request, it should return an EmscriptenResponse whose body can be read incrementally and behaves like a read-only, non-seekable raw stream.
Given a JSPI streaming response, when the stream reaches EOF or is closed by the caller, it should close cleanly and future reads should produce end-of-stream behavior.

Given Node.js launched with Pyodide async execution and the required WebAssembly stack-switching support, when a caller makes a urllib3 request, it should complete through the JSPI fetch path for both buffered and streaming responses.

Given Node.js without usable JSPI, when a caller attempts a buffered or streaming urllib3 request, it should raise _RequestError that identifies the missing runtime capability instead of attempting an unsupported browser transport.
Given any JSPI request stage with a positive timeout, when the timeout expires before the JavaScript promise resolves, urllib3 should abort the request and raise _TimeoutError.
Given a JSPI fetch or stream read that fails for a non-timeout JavaScript reason, urllib3 should raise _RequestError while preserving available request and response context.
Given a non-JSPI browser Emscripten runtime, when existing buffered or worker-based streaming requests are made, they should continue to follow the pre-existing fallback behavior.

task_4.title: Make connection exceptions pickleable
task_4.description: urllib3 2.3.0 adds serialization support for two connection-related exception types that previously could not be pickled. This allows applications that pass, cache, or persist exceptions through Python pickling to handle NewConnectionError and NameResolutionError without serialization failures, while preserving the exception class identity rather than guaranteeing complete instance state preservation.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that connection failure exceptions raised for new connection failures and DNS/name resolution failures can be serialized and deserialized with Python pickling without breaking existing exception usage.

expectation.grounded: urllib3.exceptions.NewConnectionError and urllib3.exceptions.NameResolutionError must support Python pickling and unpickling. After deserialization, the resulting object should be an instance of the same public exception class. The fix may discard detailed instance-specific data such as the original connection object, host, reason, or formatted message content during the pickle round trip.
expectation.conceptual: Applications should be able to serialize and later restore these connection-related errors without the serialization process failing, while retaining enough information to identify the kind of error that occurred.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the public exception classes, their existing construction signatures, inheritance relationships, or catchability as urllib3 exceptions. Do not require serialized NewConnectionError or NameResolutionError instances to preserve non-pickle-friendly connection state or all original diagnostic details.
constraints.conceptual: The change should make these errors portable through serialization without altering how callers create, raise, catch, or broadly classify them.

behavior: NewConnectionError instances can be pickled without raising a serialization error.
Pickle-loaded NewConnectionError values are reconstructed as NewConnectionError instances.
NameResolutionError instances can be pickled without raising a serialization error.
Pickle-loaded NameResolutionError values are reconstructed as NameResolutionError instances.
The pickle round trip is class-preserving but not state-complete; original connection, host, reason, and message details are not guaranteed to survive.
Existing runtime behavior for constructing, raising, and catching NewConnectionError and NameResolutionError remains compatible with prior usage.
acceptance_criteria: When a NewConnectionError is serialized and deserialized with Python pickle, it should complete without a serialization failure and produce a NewConnectionError object.
When a NameResolutionError is serialized and deserialized with Python pickle, it should complete without a serialization failure and produce a NameResolutionError object.
When callers catch these exceptions by their existing urllib3 exception types, the same catch behavior should continue to work.
When deserialized instances are inspected, callers should not rely on the original connection object, host, reason, or full diagnostic message being preserved.
